subject: Next steps: integration constraints and hosting path recommendation (SSO / KMS / log retention)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Patel <sasha.p@helixmed.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — integration gaps & next steps

Thanks for the time this morning, Sasha — good call. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we have alignment on constraints that drive hosting: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC / on-prem).

Key notes from HelixMed: 
- SSO: Must support SAML 2.0 with IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows; need SCIM for group provisioning later.
- KMS / HSM: Primary requirement is customer-controlled keys; HelixMed prefers HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2) and does not allow plaintext export.
- Logging & retention: Regulatory requirement to retain audit logs for 7 years; must include request-level metadata and redaction controls.

What we committed to: 
1) Rishi to outline technical options for KMS/HSM and logging retention (Dedicated vs Private implications).
2) Share a short integration matrix (SSO, KMS, logs) and hosting recommendation by EOD tomorrow.
3) Schedule a 45-min infra deep-dive with HelixMed engineering + our infra lead (suggest Wed 5/5).

Attachments: integration-matrix.xlsx (working draft), redwood-hosting-comparison.pdf

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

From: Sasha Patel <sasha.p@helixmed.com>

Cc: HelixMed Security <security@helixmed.com>, CTO Office <cto@helixmed.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — integration gaps & next steps

Thanks Neha — quick clarifications from our side so Rishi can scope: 

- KMS/HSM: We operate in AWS but our policy requires HSM-backed keys. We use AWS CloudHSM in two regions and we cannot allow key material to be exported. If the vendor cannot integrate with CloudHSM or an equivalent HSM, the only acceptable path is an on-prem/private deployment where we own the HSM.
- BYOK: We are open to BYOK if the provider can support a true HSM-backed Key Broker (no key export, attested hardware).
- Logging: Must capture request id, timestamp, calling principal, model+version, token counts, and store logs in our S3 with encryption at rest. Retention 7 years, with the ability to purge redacted content on request.

We are flexible on SSO SCIM timing (can be phase 2) but SAML + strong mTLS for service-to-service is required at go-live.

If you can summarize which hosting options satisfy each requirement — great. We also need to see SOC2 summary and any HSM integration references.

—Sasha
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Patel <sasha.p@helixmed.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — integration gaps & next steps

On Thu, Apr 28, 2027 at 9:12 AM Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Key notes from HelixMed: ... KMS / HSM: Primary requirement is customer-controlled keys; HelixMed prefers HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2) and does not allow plaintext export.

Thanks — I sketched practical options below and attached a matrix with the mapping. Short version: if HelixMed requires a true customer-managed HSM with no export, Private (VPC / on-prem) is the only path that guarantees control; Dedicated has limited BYOK options but typically relies on Cloud KMS (not CloudHSM) unless we provision a dedicated HSM appliance in-customer VPC which complicates operations.

Option A — Hosted API (fastest):
- SSO: OK (SAML + future SCIM).
- KMS: DOES NOT meet HelixMed HSM requirement — Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS; BYOK is limited and not HSM-backed.
- Logs: We can stream anonymized metadata to customer S3; full request logs with PII are restricted in Hosted.

Option B — Dedicated (reserved capacity in our cloud / tenant-isolated):
- SSO: OK.
- KMS: Supports BYOK via Cloud KMS (customer-managed keys) — but CloudKMS != CloudHSM; keys could be HSM-backed depending on cloud offering but customer still cannot physically possess HSM.
- Logs: Can route detailed logs to customer S3 with agreed retention; needs contract and retention SLAs.

Option C — Private (VPC / on-prem):
- SSO: Full control, supports SAML + SCIM in your IdP.
- KMS/HSM: Supports direct CloudHSM integration or on-prem HSM and BYOK where key material never leaves customer control.
- Logs: Full request-level logs stored in customer environment; retention policies are customer-controlled.

Recommended immediate path for HelixMed: 
- If HSM (no-export) is a blocking requirement: proceed to Private deployment. We can propose a phased Private setup: initial VPC-deployed cluster integrated with your CloudHSM (or HSM appliance) and log export to your S3 with 7-year retention.
- If HelixMed can accept CloudKMS with strict IAM + attestations: Dedicated could be an acceptable compromise (lower operational lift).

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical deep-dive (45 min) to validate CloudHSM connectivity/networking and log export requirements.
2) Share SOC2 summary and integration playbook (attached SOC2-summary.pdf).
3) If Private is needed, schedule infra kickoff to scope deployment effort and lead time.

Attachment: integration-matrix.xlsx (detailed mapping)

—Rishi
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Sasha — thanks for the clear constraints and the security team CC. 

Summary of proposed plan and asks: 
- If HelixMed confirms "no key export / HSM mandatory" we will mark Private deployment as the required path and pull in our Private deployment leads.
- If HelixMed can accept CloudKMS with attestation, we will evaluate Dedicated as a lower-cost alternative and share configuration controls.

Please confirm two items before our infra deep-dive: 
1) Which CloudHSM regions are in scope and whether you can run a peering/VPN to allow our VPC-to-VPC connectivity for initial integration.
2) Point person from your security team for the 45-min call (we need network, KMS owner, and retention owner).

I attached the integration matrix and hosting comparison for your review. Proposed time for infra call: Wed 2027-05-05 10:00 AM PT — does that work?

Thanks — will follow up with scheduling once you confirm.

Neha
